A more cynical person might respond that, if whales can not survive against the apex predator known as man, they deserve extinction as much as millions of other species that went extinct when facing superior predators. That humans are extremely efficient at driving other species into extinction while transforming the environment to fit their respective needs (or what they believe to be their respective needs) is a mere variable that matters little in the bigger picture. An even more cynical person might argue that, if humans have no particular need for whales, then they have no particular obligation to keep the whales alive, either.

Whales and similiar species such as dolphins may be highly intelligent and capable of feeling great suffering, but technically speaking, so are pigs. This is not to say that I believe neither species holds any moral rights whatsoever - I would prefer to limit the suffering of both as much as possible - but unless one plans to go entirely vegan (and even then, even plants do feel something akin to pain), I still think that the main argument against hunting whales should be that there's not awfully many of them left, and that we plainly can not breed such large animals as we can do with pigs.
